threads.name: Rockefeller's Influence on the Met's Collections
threads.description: This theme explores how Nelson A. Rockefeller and the Rockefeller family significantly contributed to the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collections, particularly in the 20th century. It begins with Nelson A. Rockefeller's donation in 1969, turns with the opening of the Michael C. Rockefeller Wing in 1982, and pays off with the lasting impact of these contributions on the museum's global art collections.

threads.name: Development of Cultural Collections at the Met
threads.description: This theme traces the development of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's cultural collections, influenced by key figures and events. It starts with the establishment of the Department of Far Eastern Art in 1915, turns with the contributions of donors like J. Pierpont Morgan, and concludes with the integration of diverse cultural artifacts, highlighting the museum's dedication to representing global art traditions.

threads.name: The Met's Expansion in the 20th Century
threads.description: This theme examines the Metropolitan Museum of Art's expansion during the 20th century, marked by significant acquisitions and the establishment of new departments. It begins with the founding of the museum in 1870, turns with the opening of the arts of Africa, Oceania, and the Americas in 1982, and culminates in the museum's vast collection by 2000.
